clue.text: Punishment given by Nym, perhaps

parts.note: Nym is a soldier of that rank in Shakespeare's Henry V, so the punishment he hands out is named after his rank, the word that also describes beating

explanation.surface: A question about what discipline a Shakespearean character would dish out.
explanation.walkthrough: Nym, Falstaff's crony in Henry V and The Merry Wives of Windsor, holds the rank in the answer; the same word describes physical punishment, as in a caning.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical chastisement of the body is called by this adjective, which is also a junior army rank such as Nym's.

clue.text: Personal magnetism of Mrs Mopp, one of one's relations

parts.note: Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the wartime radio comedy ITMA, so a char
one's stands for one is, I'S
one of one's relations is ma, mother

explanation.surface: The charm of an office cleaner who is a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp, from the 1940s BBC radio show ITMA, is the classic cleaning lady, a char in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm that draws and inspires others is a kind of personal pull.

clue.text: No creed, it turns out, is so esoteric

indicators.note: turns out signals that the letters of no creed it come out in another order

explanation.surface: A creedless belief system proves to be obscure.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite knowledge is obscure, known only to a few.

clue.text: Indecorous, turning tail in the target area

indicators.note: turning tail means the last two letters of the word for indecorous are switched round

parts.note: outre means beyond the bounds of propriety

explanation.surface: Someone behaving badly flees from a shooting range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' swaps the last pair of OUTRE, RE becoming ER. 'turning tail' looks like running away.
explanation.definitionFit: On an archery or rifle target, the ring furthest from the bull carries this name.

clue.text: Bring forward a price rise

definitions.meaning: to move a date or proposal earlier or onward
an increase in the cost of something

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means move onward or earlier, and as a noun it is an increase in value.

clue.text: Fish thrown back to beast? Not all of it

indicators.note: thrown back tells us to read the whole run of letters from the end to the start
not all of the beast's synonym is used: its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a brute is a beast

explanation.surface: A fish is tossed back to some creature, but only part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not all of it' drops the beast's last letter; 'thrown back' turns the whole run, giving TOBRUT read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized for the table.

clue.text: Abnormal, not like Linnaeus's history

parts.note: un- is a prefix meaning not
Linnaeus, the Swedish botanist, worked in natural history

explanation.surface: Something odd, unlike the story of the great botanist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something contrary to nature is out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Celebration at which a runner possibly needs oxygen

parts.note: a runner bean is a climbing bean, so a runner is an example of a bean
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An athlete at a party gasping for oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' looks like an athlete needing air; it is a runner bean. BEANO is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a jolly party or knees-up.

clue.text: Doing one's best to be tiresome

explanation.definitionFit: Making an attempt is the present participle, and an irritating person is likewise wearing.

clue.text: Customer's right in courts? Not ours

indicators.note: in means the right is placed inside the abbreviation for court

parts.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A shopper's legal rights in foreign courts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not ours' hints that the customer is someone else's, a lawyer's rather than our own.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who pays for a professional's services is a patron of the firm.

clue.text: Where a street is without gas in Berkshire

definitions.text: Where a street is without gas in Berkshire

indicators.note: is without means the letters for a street sit outside, enclosing the gas

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide, a gas

explanation.surface: A Berkshire road with no gas supply.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a town in Berkshire, a county west of London, famous for its royal racecourse; the whole clue both builds and describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The racecourse town sits in the English county of Berkshire.

clue.text: It may introduce a service maintained by private donations

definitions.meaning: an organ solo played before a church service is called by this name
a body funded by gifts rather than the state, such as a charity hospital, is described this way

explanation.definitionFit: An organ piece opening worship carries the name, and the adjective describes organisations funded by gifts rather than taxes.

clue.text: One caring, possibly, for the state of the green?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of one caring could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A groundsman who looks after the golf green or village lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ONE CARING. The 'green' looks like grass, but it means inexperienced, and the state of being green is not knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being green means raw and inexperienced, so its condition is a lack of knowledge.

clue.text: Tree (or shrub) found in Bath (or Norwich)

indicators.note: found in tells us the answer lies within the run of letters of the two city names

explanation.surface: A tree or bush that grows in two English cities.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across baTH OR Norwich; the brackets are only punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn and blackthorn are spiny trees or shrubs commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Old coin and note wrapped in watered silk

indicators.note: wrapped in means the note is placed inside the fabric

parts.note: moire is silk with a rippled, watered sheen
do (doh) is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An antique coin and a banknote kept wrapped in a piece of fine silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' wants to be a banknote alongside the coin; it is the sol-fa note DO.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a Portuguese gold piece current in England in the 18th century.

clue.text: Bad season for one's descendants

parts.note: off means bad, as of food gone rotten
spring is a season

explanation.surface: A poor year for the next generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Children and their line of descent are a person's progeny.

clue.text: Quarrel about a king's system of taxation

indicators.note: about means the quarrel word goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tiff is a petty quarrel
R, for rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A dispute over a monarch's tax regime.
explanation.definitionFit: A schedule of duties or charges levied on goods is a tax scheme.

clue.text: Was alarmed about the state of a 27, for example

indicators.note: about means the alarmed word goes round the word the

parts.note: feared means was afraid

explanation.surface: Someone frightened about the condition of a city in Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 looks like the city, but means the Baltimore oriole, a bird, whose state is having plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Having plumage is the condition of any bird, such as the Baltimore oriole.

clue.text: The pony 29's leader breaks for a beginner

indicators.note: breaks signals that the pony's letters are broken up and rearranged
leader picks the first letter of the answer at 29

parts.note: 29 across is the flag and naval officer

explanation.surface: A novice breaking in a pony led by a flag officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' rearranges THE PONY with E, the first letter of ENSIGN.
explanation.definitionFit: A novice or new convert is someone just starting out.

clue.text: Changes here among the bats?

parts.note: changes are sequences rung on church bells, and bats proverbially live in a church tower, as in 'bats in the ...'

explanation.definitionFit: A bell tower is where bell-ringers ring changes, and the idiom has bats living there.

clue.text: In a tree, many see 21 dn

indicators.note: In means the letters for many and see go inside the tree

parts.note: a yew is a tree
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, taken as many
lo is an old word for see or behold

explanation.surface: A crowd spotting colour among the branches.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 dn is the colouring matter at 21 down, and this is one such colour.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one hue among the many colouring matters.

clue.text: Fell European with weapon

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
an axe is a weapon

explanation.surface: A European attacks someone with a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' is the verb meaning knock down, not a hill or an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike down with a heavy blow, as with a butcher's axe, is to fell.

clue.text: Animal intended, we hear, to provide colouring matter

parts.note: a pig is an animal

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for intended is taken by its sound

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A creature designed to supply paint.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that gives colour to paint or tissue is a colourant.

clue.text: Posh fur at one's disposal

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in Nancy Mitford's U and non-U
sable is a fur

explanation.surface: An elegant fur coat at your service.
explanation.definitionFit: Something available for use is serviceable.

clue.text: Organization for group riding

parts.note: a set is a group
a jockey riding is said to be up on the horse

explanation.surface: A club arranged for people riding together.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrangement or structure of an organisation is its set-up.

clue.text: Legal writs served for malicious reports?

definitions.meaning: writs for summoning extra jurors when the panel is short
gossip or tittle-tattle spread to cause trouble

explanation.definitionFit: Jury-summoning writs bear this Latin-derived name, and it also means gossip told to make mischief.

clue.text: Its illuminating warning aggravated his plight

indicators.note: aggravated suggests the plight was stirred up, so its letters along with his are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning light that only made a man's predicament worse.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon warns ships of danger with its light.

clue.text: Character given by the Army

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Moral fibre instilled by military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like personality, but means a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Old Lithuanian land-owner introducing one other in Maryland

indicators.note: introducing means the Lithuanian comes first and leads in what follows

parts.note: the Balts were an ancient people whose descendants include the Lithuanians
I is the Roman numeral one
more means other or additional

explanation.surface: A Lithuanian landowner of old brings another person to Maryland.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Baltimore was the proprietor granted Maryland by charter; 'in Maryland' places him and hints at the city of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Calvert barons holding this title were proprietors of the colony of Maryland.

clue.text: Almost executed before the time appointed

indicators.note: executed here means beheaded, so the word for almost loses its head letter

parts.note: nearly means almost

explanation.surface: A man was all but put to death ahead of schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: Arriving ahead of schedule is being premature.

clue.text: Flying officer?

parts.note: the clue suggests an RAF rank, but means a flag that flies, which is also the name of a junior naval officer

explanation.definitionFit: A national flag flown on ships and a junior commissioned officer share this name.

clue.text: Right to return on horseback — best ride when together

definitions.meaning: on the stock exchange this is a double option, a right either to call for stock or to deliver it back

definitions.text: on horseback — best ride when together
definitions.meaning: joined up, best ride makes bestride, to sit astride a horse with legs on either side

explanation.definitionFit: The stock-exchange option is so called, and the verb means to sit with legs either side, as a rider on a horse.
